promptLatex: How many positive integer solutions does x + y + z = 8 have?
hintLatex:
For positive integer solutions, give one star to each variable first, leaving n-k stars to distribute freely.
The formula is \binom{n-1}{k-1}. Here n = 8 and k = 3, so \binom{7}{2}.
solutionLatex:
For positive integer solutions, give one unit to each variable first. This uses 3 units, leaving 8 - 3 = 5 stars to distribute freely among 3 variables.

The number of solutions is \binom{5+3-1}{3-1} = \binom{7}{2} = 21.
